questions.prompt: What is the order aggregate in this order system, and how does the code stop callers from bypassing its rules?

keyPoints.text: An aggregate is a group of related values whose rules must stay consistent through an operation.
keyPoints.quote: An aggregate is a group of related values with rules that must stay consistent through an operation.

keyPoints.text: For an order that group is item quantities, price snapshots, discount, status and total.
keyPoints.quote: an order's item quantities, price snapshots, discount, status, and total belong together.

keyPoints.text: Mutating a line returned by getItems would bypass the rules.
keyPoints.quote: Allowing callers to mutate a line returned by `getItems` would bypass those rules.

keyPoints.text: An unmodifiable list is not enough when the items inside are shared mutable objects.
keyPoints.quote: Even an unmodifiable list is insufficient if the contained items are still mutable shared objects.

keyPoints.text: Returned items are detached copies, so changing one does not change the stored order.
Changes go through service.updateItemQuantity, the intended update path.
keyPoints.quote: The intended update path is `service.updateItemQuantity(orderId, productId, quantity)`.

questions.prompt: How does a quantity change keep the discount valid, and why are totals derived rather than stored?

keyPoints.text: The aggregate builds a candidate line with the existing name and unit price and computes the proposed subtotal first.
keyPoints.quote: The aggregate builds a candidate line using the existing name and unit price, computes the proposed subtotal, and checks the discount before replacing the line.

keyPoints.text: If a reduction would make the subtotal smaller than the discount, the command is rejected.
keyPoints.quote: If a quantity reduction would make subtotal smaller than the discount, it rejects the command.

keyPoints.text: The user must lower the discount explicitly; the discount is no longer changed as a side effect.
keyPoints.quote: the application no longer silently changes a discount as a side effect of recalculation.

keyPoints.text: Subtotal is the sum of line totals and total is subtotal minus discount, so fewer facts must be kept in sync.
keyPoints.quote: Derived totals reduce the number of facts that must be kept synchronized.

keyPoints.text: Merging more of the same product keeps the existing line's price snapshot.
keyPoints.quote: Merging another quantity of the same product keeps that existing snapshot.

questions.prompt: Why is restoring a saved order different from replaying user commands, and which workflow rules apply to status?

keyPoints.text: Restoration is not the same as applying user commands.
keyPoints.quote: Restoration is not the same as applying user commands.

keyPoints.text: A paid order loaded from disk must regain its items and discount without reopening it or changing its update time.
keyPoints.quote: A paid order loaded from disk must regain its existing items and discount without reopening it for editing or changing its saved update time.

keyPoints.text: Order.restore accepts the complete item collection and validates the resulting state directly.
keyPoints.quote: `Order.restore` therefore accepts a complete collection and validates the resulting state directly.

keyPoints.text: Transitions: DRAFT to SUBMITTED or CANCELLED, SUBMITTED to PAID or CANCELLED, PAID to SHIPPED or CANCELLED; SHIPPED and CANCELLED are terminal.
Only DRAFT and SUBMITTED permit content edits.
keyPoints.quote: Only DRAFT and SUBMITTED permit content edits.

keyPoints.text: SUBMITTED, PAID and SHIPPED require items, and a submitted order cannot lose its final item.
keyPoints.quote: SUBMITTED, PAID, and SHIPPED require items, and a submitted order cannot lose its final item.

keyPoints.text: None of these protections supplies authenticated ownership, concurrency handling, stale-write detection or payment idempotency.
keyPoints.quote: None of these supplies authenticated ownership, concurrent request handling, cross-process stale-write detection, or payment idempotency.
